Thanks again for the product walkthrough yesterday. Per our call, I put together an initial node-mapping and options matrix for the Dedicated commitment you asked about. High level: H100s give headroom for long-context requests and memory-heavy KV cache; A100 is a good midline for throughput with reasonable memory; L4 is cost-effective for short-context/low-memory inference and burst traffic.

Attached: node_mapping_v1.xlsx (sketch) — contains three scenarios (latency-first, cost-first, hybrid-reserve).

A couple of quick questions to make the sizing precise:
- Typical request profile (tokens): median prompt+response ~ 300 tokens, 95th pct ~ 2k tokens?
- Concurrency target at peak QPS? (you mentioned a 99th p99 latency SLA of ~250ms for search reranking)
- Long-context usage: how many requests need >8k context and how large is the KV cache per session?
- Procurement timeline and preferred commit term (12/24 months)?

My ask: if you can confirm the above this week we’ll firm up a hybrid proposal with explicit node counts and run the cost/latency curves.

Sean/Monica — drafted a recommended configuration based on Caroline's profile. Major points:

1) Hybrid reserve + burst model (recommended)
- Reserve: 6 H100 nodes (memory-heavy, each node handles long-context/document workflows and hosts the persistent KV caches). This protects the 10% long-context traffic and supports 400MB/session caches with margin.
- Mid-tier: 12 A100 nodes (steady throughput, model variants for standard generation and reranking).
- Burst pool: 40 L4 instances (stateless, fast warmup, cost-efficient for short requests and bursty traffic)

2) Autoscale & fallthrough policy
- Primary routing: long-context -> H100 pool; normal generation -> A100 pool; short/fallthrough -> L4.
- Autoscale multiplier: reserve handles baseline 60% of expected sustained QPS; burst pool covers up to 2.5x spikes.

3) Cost/latency tradeoffs (ballpark numbers)
- H100 reserve: higher $/hour but reduces p95/p99 latency for long-context by ~40-60% vs A100 for >16k sequences.
- A100 mid-tier: best cost/throughput balance for majority of requests.
- L4 burst: ~3-4x cheaper per token for short-context generation but limited memory (unsuitable for KV heavy sessions).

4) Operational notes
- Prefetching/kv-caching: keep KV caches pinned on H100 nodes to avoid rehydration penalties.
- Quantization: consider FP16/INT8 on A100 and L4 for cost; reserve H100 as full-precision for high-fidelity long-context ops.
- Backfill: allow automated fallback A100 -> L4 for low-memory requests if cost/latency target dictates.

Attachment: proposed_reserve_mix.pdf (one-page diagram + node counts).

If we roll this to a MAP, I propose the following commitment: 18 guaranteed GPU nodes across pools (weighted) with a 12-month term, plus a 6-month burst credit bucket to smooth seasonality. I can draft a slotting table and run estimated monthly MRR.

-Karthik
Principal Infrastructure Architect | Redwood Inference
